note: Content library for the sphere's tap → curated pick (Cycle II MVP). 200 lines, all 8 moments, researched for a 14–30 audience (original 'sharp friend' voice + Stoic/Goggins/Mamba/Biles energies; real quotes public-domain only). Text-only, self-contained, chosen by a tiny deterministic matcher — no server, no keys, no external calls. Ships inside the app repo when built. See README.md.
voice: A sharp friend in your corner, not a motivational poster. Honest, a little wry, practical in the moment. Respects the reader's intelligence. Never saccharine, never preachy, no hollow hype. Plain human language — no em-dash chains, no rule-of-three, no 'not just X'.

moments.crave: Resisting an urge — the candy, the cigarette, the scroll. Ride the wave.
moments.start: Can't get going. Activation energy. Lower the bar and move.
moments.grind: Mid-task and it hurts — the cold shower, the last set. Stay in it.
moments.doubt: The why has gone quiet. Meaning dip. Keep the promise, the reason comes back.
moments.tired: Low on energy. Permission to go small without breaking the chain.
moments.win: Just checked in. Sit in it, bank it, come back tomorrow.
moments.slip: Missed a day or broke it. Self-compassion, then get back up.
moments.any: The commitment itself, any moment. The dot just wants today.

schema: Each line: {id, moment, category, phase, source, text, voice?}. moment = the 8 buckets above (what the user is feeling). category = the challenge flavour (any | sugar | smoke | drink | move | calm | cold | focus | read); most lines are 'any', a few are flavoured to show the axis. phase = any | early | mid | late (where in the week). source = null for original Stakes lines, or the attributed author for a real quote (public-domain only). voice = optional energy tag for an original line that channels a researched figure (stoic | goggins | mamba | biles); no modern figure is ever quoted verbatim.

voices.note: Researched for a 14–30 audience (Aug 2026). The BASE is the original 'sharp friend' voice — this audience trusts people they know over celebrities and rejects performative hustle-culture, so famous names SEASON, they don't dominate. Real quotes are public-domain only (the Stoics); modern figures are CHANNELLED as energy in original lines, never fabricated as quotes.

roster.who: The Stoics — Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, Epictetus
roster.why: Real Gen-Z resurgence (Daily Stoic, 257k+ TikTok videos). Pragmatic: control what you can, react not event. Public-domain, so verbatim-safe.
His thesis is ours: discipline over motivation, do it when you don't feel like it. Huge with the audience. Channelled, not quoted.
Better-than-yesterday, show-up-tired, failure-isn't-a-verdict. Enduring, cross-demographic. Channelled.
Rest-is-strength, protect-your-mind, comeback. Balances the male-skewing energy above and matches Gen-Z's anti-toxic-positivity. Channelled.

lines.text: A craving is a wave. Wait it out. Three minutes and it breaks.
You don't have to want it less. You just have to not move for five minutes.
The urge is loud because it's losing. Loud isn't the same as strong.
Future you is already annoyed you're even considering this. Side with that guy.
It's not 'never again.' It's 'not right now.' You can do right now.
Say it out loud: 'I'm having a craving.' Watch how fast it shrinks.
Glass of water, then walk to a different room. Boring beats the urge almost every time.
The candy will still be candy tomorrow. You have better things to be.
It's not the one cigarette. It's the promise you made to yourself right before it. Keep that one.
You don't need motivation. You need to put one shoe on. Start there.
Two minutes. Promise yourself you can stop after two. You won't want to.
The hardest part is the doorway. You're already off the couch, reading this.
Nobody feels like it. The people who do it anyway are just people who did it anyway.
Make the bar stupidly low. One pushup. You'll do more because you're already down there.
Don't think about the whole thing. Think about the next thirty seconds.
Motivation shows up after you start, not before. So start, and let it catch up.
You can do it badly. Badly still counts. Badly still lights the dot.
This is the part that counts. Comfortable never built anyone.
It's meant to be hard. Hard is what you're trading for the after.
Cold water has never once actually killed a person. Your brain is bluffing.
You wanted to be someone who does hard things. Well. It's now.
Halfway hurts the most. Push through it and it starts giving back.
You can stop any time. That's exactly why finishing means something.
Breathe. The discomfort is information, not an order.
One more. Not the whole set. Just one more, then decide again.
You didn't start this because it was easy. You started it because it mattered. It still does.
One skipped day won't sink it. A skipped day becoming your default will. Guard the default.
Small and boring, repeated, beats big and impressive, abandoned.
Ask the big question later. Right now just keep the promise. The why comes back.
It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that things are difficult.
You're on day three. Day three is where most people already quit. You're not most people.
The point isn't this one day. It's becoming the kind of person who does this day. That's built right now.
Discipline is just remembering what you want. You wanted this. Check the goal if you forgot.
Tired is allowed. Quitting is a separate decision. Do the small version today.
You don't need a hundred percent. Forty counts. Forty still moves the dot.
Rest isn't the same as stopping. Take the rest. Keep the streak.
Low-energy day? Lower the goal, not the streak. Show up small.
You're running on empty and you still opened this. That's most of the battle, honestly.
Do the version you could do half-asleep. It still counts as keeping your word.
'I'm tired' has a way of showing up every single day. Be honest which one today is.
Ten minutes, then you're allowed to be done. Set a timer and go.
That's a win. Sit in it for a second. You earned the second.
Nobody's clapping, so I will. Well done. That was the hard one and you took it.
You just proved the story you tell about yourself is negotiable. Keep renegotiating.
Bank it. Come back tomorrow and take the next one.
That's the rep nobody saw. Those are the ones that actually count.
Feels good, doesn't it. Remember this the next time it's hard.
One day is one day. Seven of these is a week. It starts with the one you just did.
You showed up when you didn't have to. That's the whole game, and you just won a round.
Missed a day? A streak is a story, not a verdict. Write the next line.
One miss is a typo, not a rewrite. Keep going.
The people you look up to all have days they'd rather forget. They just didn't quit on the next one.
Be as kind to yourself as you'd be to a friend who slipped. Then get up the way you'd tell them to.
Don't let one miss cost you two. Today is the one that matters now.
The comeback is a better story than the clean run anyway. Start it.
You didn't fail. You paused. The difference is what you do in the next ten minutes.
Guilt doesn't move the dot. Showing up does. So show up.
You put your word on this. That still means something. Especially now.
The dot doesn't care how you feel. It just wants today. Give it today.
You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
The mood will pass. The choice you make inside it won't. Choose like you'll remember it.
Nothing dramatic required. Just don't break the chain today.
You're one decision away from a good day. This is the decision.
The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Whatever you decide right now, decide it on purpose. That's the whole of discipline.
The voice begging you to quit is the one you're training against. Don't take orders from it.
You can't stop the urge from showing up. You can stop it from driving.
The craving isn't yours to control. The next sixty seconds are. Own those.
We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
Motivation is a mood. Discipline is a decision you already made. Go keep it.
Nobody's coming to make you do this. That's the bad news and the entire point.
You don't have to want to. Wanting to is optional. Doing it isn't.
First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
The suck is the workout. Easy wouldn't have changed you anyway.
You're not tired. You're at the point where most people stop. That's a different thing.
Right here, where it starts to hurt, is where the person you want to be gets built.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
Goals are nice. Habits are what actually show up for you. Feed the habit today.
You don't control whether today feels meaningful. You control whether you show up for it.
Half of what's stressing you hasn't happened and won't. Deal with the day that's actually here.
The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
Show up tired. Show up bored. Show up anyway. That's the whole secret, and there isn't a bigger one.
Stepping back to protect your head isn't quitting. The strongest people you know do it on purpose.
The brave move today might be doing less, deliberately, with zero guilt.
Rest like it's part of the training. It is. Then come back and finish.
Protecting your mind isn't the soft option. It's what keeps you in the game for years.
Better than yesterday. That's the only scoreboard. Did you beat yesterday? You just did.
Greatness isn't a talent. It's this — the boring rep, done again, when skipping was right there.
You don't owe anyone a perfect streak. You owe yourself the next honest day.
You're allowed to not be okay and still keep your word in a small way. Both are true at once.
The obsession people romanticize is just this: you did the thing again today. So do it again.
The event already happened. The only thing left is your response. Make it a good one.
Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
No man is free who is not master of himself.
Half the time the craving isn't even about the thing. Eat something, text someone, then check if it's still there.
It promises relief and hands you ten quiet minutes and then guilt. You've seen this film. You know how it ends.
You're not saying no. You're saying 'in twenty minutes.' In twenty minutes you won't care.
You're not a person who caves at 9pm. Prove it one more night.
Every time you don't, it gets quieter tomorrow. You're not just winning tonight, you're turning down the volume for good.
The craving has one move, and it's making it right now. You've got the entire rest of the playbook.
Stand up. Cravings hate movement. Two minutes of literally anything else and it loosens its grip.
You are not your urges. You're the thing that gets to tell them no.
Sit in it for sixty seconds and actually feel it. It's nowhere near as big as it's pretending to be.
One drink was never the plan. The plan was the person you're becoming. Stay with the plan.
'Just this once' is how streaks actually die. It is never just once, and some part of you already knows that.
The feed will still be infinite in an hour. It's the one thing you never have to worry about running out of.
Wanting it isn't the failure. Doing it is the only line that counts, and you haven't crossed it.
Give your hands or your mouth something else to do. Dumb little trick. Works anyway.
This is 9pm sugar-brain talking. It wants the thing at the exact hour you're weakest. Don't take meetings with it now.
Count down from five and move on one. Don't give your brain time to file the objection.
The bigger the drag you feel, the more it's usually worth doing. Resistance points right at the thing.
Do it now and future you gets to relax. Skip it and future you inherits the debt, with interest.
Put what you need in your hand. Half of starting is just clearing the next excuse out of the way.
There's no better moment coming. This is the moment. It's a bit inconvenient, and that's completely fine.
You don't need a plan for the whole day. You need the first move. The rest tends to follow it.
The ones you admire aren't more motivated. They just stopped holding a debate about it every single morning.
If the goal feels heavy, it's too big for right now. Cut it in half. Then in half again. Start there.
Say the excuse out loud. If it sounds thin, that's because it is. Go.
You don't have to feel ready. You just have to start the little ritual that makes the rest automatic.
You control the first step and nothing after it. Lucky for you, the first step was the whole problem.
The couch is comfortable and undefeated and will still be right here when you get back. Go.
Do what you can, with what you have, where you are.
Begin badly. Begin slowly. Begin annoyed. Just begin — momentum can't help you until you do.
Stop counting what's left. Count what you've already banked. You're further along than it feels.
Push past the first 'I want to stop.' There's almost always more in the tank than the thought admits.
Learn the line between hurts and harms. This hurts. It is not harming you. Keep going.
In an hour you'll be so glad you didn't stop here. Borrow that feeling and spend it now.
Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.
The rep you don't want is the only one that changes anything. Everything before it was warm-up.
Your body could keep going for ages. It's your brain writing cheques your legs can easily cash. Ignore it.
Don't look at the summit. Look at the next step, then the next. That's how everyone who's climbed one did it.
This isn't happening to you. You walked in here on purpose. Act like someone who chose it.
Thirty seconds. You've survived worse before breakfast. In you go, out you come, prouder.
Every worthwhile thing has a boring middle. The middle is exactly where most people quit, and where it's actually being built.
You can't see progress from inside one day. Trust the days you already stacked. They're real even when the feeling isn't.
You set this goal for a reason your calmer self believed in. Borrow their conviction for ten minutes.
Comparison is a great way to feel behind in a race nobody else is running. Run yours.
If there is no struggle, there is no progress.
You fell in love with the result. Fall in love with the reps instead. The result takes care of itself.
Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views they take of them.
Meaning isn't a feeling that arrives. It's the thing you build by not quitting on the days it goes quiet.
You don't have to believe in it today. You just have to not quit on it today. Belief comes back later.
You've already paid for the days you did. Quitting now is the one move that actually wastes them.
Talk to yourself like a coach, not a critic. The critic has never once helped anyone finish anything.
Motivation is a fair-weather friend. It left the second this got hard. Good thing you brought discipline, who stayed.
You're not behind. There's no schedule. There's just the next day, and whether you show up for it.
The goal didn't change just because your mood did. Do today's piece of it. Mood doesn't get to manage you.
Do the smallest honest version. A walk instead of a run is still not quitting, and not quitting is the game.
You're probably not out of willpower. You're out of blood sugar and sleep. Eat, drink, then decide.
Some days, keeping the streak alive is the entire win. Alive is enough today.
Listen to the tired. Sometimes it's an excuse, sometimes it's your body being honest. Get good at telling them apart.
Tired is just the tax on wanting something real. Pay it and keep the thing.
Rough day? It ends at midnight. You don't have to fix everything, just get through to a clean one.
You don't have to be impressive today. You just have to be here. And you're here.
You can't control how much is left in the tank. You can control what you do with it. Spend a little.
You've done harder on less sleep. This is a Tuesday. Do the small version, then go to bed proud.
That's another one in a row. Chains are easy to keep and a pain to restart. Don't make yourself restart.
Every time you do this you cast a vote for who you're becoming. That was another one in the right box.
Motivation said no today and you did it anyway. That's the good kind of evidence about yourself. Keep it.
Nobody remembers the ones you skip. This one you'll feel in a month. Stack it.
It doesn't feel like much on its own. None of them do. That's the trick — they add up while you're not watching.
Look at you. Keeping promises to yourself like some kind of functional adult.
Winning's a habit too, and you just made it a little more automatic. Same time tomorrow.
No fireworks. Just a small, true 'I did what I said I'd do.' That quiet feeling is the entire point.
Someone who follows you needs to see this is possible. Post it. You might just start them.
You showed up as you were today, not as your best self, and did it anyway. That one counts double.
Remember this next time the voice says you always quit. It's on the record now that you don't.
That's the discipline compounding. Boring today. Unstoppable in a year. Keep feeding it.
Day one is the heaviest one you'll ever lift, and it's behind you now. It gets a little lighter from here.
Take the two seconds. You did a hard thing on purpose. Most people didn't manage that today.
Never miss twice. One miss is just life. Two in a row is how a new, worse habit quietly starts.
You'd forgive a friend for this without blinking. Extend yourself the same courtesy, then get moving.
A missed day is information, not a character flaw. What made it hard? Fix that, not yourself.
The greats miss too. The only real difference is how fast they get back to work. So get back to work.
The miss cost you one day. The shame spiral is trying to charge you five more. Don't pay it.
Draw a line. Everything before it is done and gone. The only day you can win is the one in front of you.
It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.
You didn't break the streak. You interrupted it. Streaks resume. Start the new one right now.
Alright, that day happened. Filing it under 'human.' Moving on.
Falling down isn't the story. Everyone falls. What you do in the next hour is the story. Write a good one.
You made a deal with yourself. Be the kind of person who keeps those. It's most of who you actually are.
You don't need a heroic day. You need an ordinary one, done. Ordinary, repeated, is the whole thing.
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste much of it.
Don't break the chain. That's the entire strategy, and it's quietly undefeated.
This is how self-respect gets built: you say you'll do a thing, then you do it. Repeat until you believe it.
Confine yourself to the present.
Be a little better than you were yesterday. Do that enough times and people start calling it talent.
You'll never regret keeping this promise. You have regretted breaking it. Let that do the deciding.
The past streak is a memory and the future one's a fantasy. There's only today, and today is doable.
No one's watching and no one's making you. That's the exact thing that makes it count when you do it anyway.
You're not chasing perfect. You're building consistent. Perfect quits at the first crack. Consistent finishes.
The man who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones.
The dot is simple. It wants one thing. Give the dot its thing and the rest of your day gets easier.
Small promise, kept. That's the rep that quietly rebuilds your trust in yourself. Do it again tomorrow.
Consistency is the flex nobody posts about. Do the unglamorous thing again today.
Future you is watching this decision. Give them something to be grateful for.
The only part of today you actually control is what you do next. Handy, because that's the whole ask.
Nothing about this has to be dramatic. Quiet and done beats loud and skipped, every single time.
Momentum is fragile and precious. One more day protects everything you've already built. Protect it.
You've done this before. You know how. Stop deliberating and go be the person who already decided.
